1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep

/-!
# Category-correct ambient contract for the rank-one Picard route

The rank-one locus lives in degree `genus C`, not in `pic0`. This module installs the concrete
ambient maps that the later open-locus restriction must consume:

* `abelDivAffTrans` maps the widened degree-`n` divisor functor to `picDegLayerFunctor C n`;
* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;
* `abelDivAffGenusSigma` specializes the map using the canonical genus representation.

The future public `PicRankOneOpen` must therefore be a subfunctor of
`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {n : ℕ}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C n) in
/-- The widened Abel transformation into the intrinsic degree-`n` Picard layer. -/
def abelDivAffTrans : divFunctorAff C n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ) where
  app T := ↾fun s => ⟨abelDivAff' C n T.unop s, fun K _ _ t => degAt_abelDivAff' s t⟩
  naturality T T' g := by
    ext s
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    exact (picEtMap_abelDivAff' g.unop s).symm

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffTrans_app_coe
    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
    ((abelDivAffTrans C n).app T s).1 = abelDivAff' C n T.unop s :=
  rfl

variable (C n) in
/-- Extend a represented widened Abel map from the slice over `Spec k` to the big site. -/
def abelDivAffSigma {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) :
    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ)) :=
  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (abelDivAffTrans C n)

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_fst {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).1 = x ≫ D.hom :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_coe {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).2.1 =
      abelDivAff' C n (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)) :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- The ambient genus-degree Abel map on the canonical represented widened divisor scheme.

This is the map that the future rank-one divisor open must restrict. It is not itself claimed to
be an open immersion. -/
def abelDivAffGenusSigma :
    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
  abelDivAffSigma C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C)

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

69	re-packaged through `Units.ext`). -/
70	private lemma unitsRestrict_unit_mul (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
71	    (i j l : D.index) :
72	    (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
73	        (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
74	        (D.unit i j)
75	      * (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
76	          (D.unit j l)
77	      = (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
78	          (D.unit i l) :=

81	/-- **The datum inverse** (worksheet GAP-1): the same basic-open cover data with the
82	termwise-inverted transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`. The cocycle law inverts termwise —
83	the units are honest `Units`, and the section rings are commutative. -/
84	noncomputable def inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
85	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π where
86	  toBasicOpenCoverData := D.toBasicOpenCoverData
87	  unit i j := (D.unit i j)⁻¹
88	  isGluingCocycle := by
89	    constructor
90	    · intro i
91	      rw [show D.unit i i = 1 from Units.ext (D.isGluingCocycle.unit_self i), inv_one,
92	        Units.val_one]
93	    · intro i j l
94	      have key : ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
95	            (inf_le_left :
96	              D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
97	            (D.unit i j))⁻¹
98	          * ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
99	              (D.unit j l))⁻¹
100	          = ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
101	              (D.unit i l))⁻¹ := by
102	        rw [← mul_inv]
103	        exact congrArg (·⁻¹) (D.unitsRestrict_unit_mul i j l)
104	      have hval := congrArg Units.val key
105	      rw [Units.val_mul] at hval
106	      exact hval

116	by subordinated cocycles on `D`'s canonical pointed cover by pieces, where the
117	subordinated cocycle of the inverse datum is the inverse cocycle. -/
118	theorem cechPicClass_inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
119	    D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := by
120	  have hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B,
121	      D.pointedCover.opens x ≤ D.inv.pieces (D.pieceIndex x) :=
122	    fun _ => le_rfl
123	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ
124	      = (gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
125	          (fun _ => le_rfl))⁻¹ := by
126	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
127	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, inv_unitsEvInf, gluedSubordCocycle_evInf]
128	    exact Units.ext rfl
129	  calc D.inv.cechPicClass
130	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
131	          (gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
132	            hσ).class :=
133	        (D.inv.cechPicClass_eq_mk D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ).symm
134	    _ = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
135	          ((gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
136	            (fun _ => le_rfl)).class)⁻¹ := by
137	        rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_inv]
138	    _ = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := rfl

158	  · rfl

169	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
170	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0)⁻¹ = 1

227	/-- The value-level matching law of the equation components against the inverted ratio
228	units: `f_i = (f_j/f_i)⁻¹ · f_j` on any open below the piece overlap. -/
229	private lemma res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul (i j : A.index) {O : (relCurve C R).Opens}
230	    (hO : O ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :
231	    (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_left) (A.eqn i)
232	      = (relCurve C R).resHom hO
233	          (((A.eqnRatio i j)⁻¹ : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
234	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
235	        * (relCurve C R).resHom (hO.trans inf_le_right) (A.eqn j) := by
236	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hO) (A.eqn_mul_eqnRatio i j)
237	  rw [map_mul] at key
238	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
239	  -- key : `res f_i · res (f_j/f_i) = res f_j` on `O`; divide by the restricted unit
240	  refine (Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq
241	    ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hO (A.eqnRatio i j))).mpr ?_
242	  rw [mul_comm]
243	  exact key

245	/-- The matching condition of the equation components for the divisor datum, in the
246	exact shape of the `gluedSubmodule` carrier at `W = ⊤` (adaptation-index form; each
247	datum-index case is definitionally this statement). -/
248	private lemma canon_matching (i j : A.index) :
249	    (relCurve C R).resHom
250	        (inf_le_left : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i)
251	        ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
252	      = (relCurve C R).resHom
253	          (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right :
254	            ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
255	          (((A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j)⁻¹ :
256	              Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)ˣ) :
257	            Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j))
258	        * (relCurve C R).resHom
259	            (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right :
260	              ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j)
261	            ((relCurve C R).resHom (inf_le_right : ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j)
262	              (A.eqn j)) := by
263	  rw [A.thetaIdealUnit_zero i j]
264	  have key := A.res_eqn_eq_inv_eqnRatio_mul i j
265	    (O := ⊤ ⊓ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)
266	    (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right)
267	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
268	  exact key
269	
270	/-- **The canonical section of the divisor datum is the equation system itself**
271	(worksheet §2 (N2)): the components `A.eqn j`, restricted to the pieces, form a
272	matching family for the inverted ratio units — a global section of the divisor
273	datum's glued sheaf. -/
274	noncomputable def canonSection :
275	    ↥(_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSubmodule R A.divisorDatum.pieces
276	        A.divisorDatum.unit ⊤) :=
277	  ⟨fun j => (relCurve C R).resHom
278	      (inf_le_right.trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)))
279	      (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)),
280	    by
281	      intro i j
282	      rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
283	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
284	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inl i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)
285	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inl j.down)
286	      · exact A.canon_matching (Sum.inr i.down) (Sum.inr j.down)⟩
287	
288	/-- The components of the canonical section are the (piece-restricted) equations. -/
289	lemma component_canonSection (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) :
290	    A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j
291	      = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j))
292	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) :=
293	  Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _
294	
295	/-- The canonical section is germ-regular: its components are the adaptation's own
296	regular equations (`eqn_regular`) — the `hreg` input of `sectionLocalEquations`,
297	with no fibrewise hypothesis. -/
298	theorem germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors
299	    (j : (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index) (y : relCurve C R)
300	    (hy : y ∈ A.divisorDatum.pieces j) :
301	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
302	        (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
303	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk y) := by
304	  have hy' : y ∈ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j) :=
305	    (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 j)) hy
306	  have hswap : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.divisorDatum.pieces j) y hy).hom
307	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection j)
308	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) y hy').hom
309	          (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 j)) := by
310	    rw [A.component_canonSection j]
311	    exact TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _
312	  rw [hswap]
313	  exact A.eqn_regular (A.lowerIndex 0 j) y hy'
314	
315	/-- **(N2) — the canonical section cuts back `d` by pure refinement**: the
316	`LocalEquations` datum cut by the canonical section on any pointed cover subordinated
317	to the pieces is `DivEq` to `d`. The common refinement is `𝒲 ⊓ d.cover`, and the
318	comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units (`relUnit`) — no fibre
319	argument anywhere. -/
320	theorem divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection
321	    (𝒲 : (relCurve C R).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C R → (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).index)
322	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C R, 𝒲.opens y ≤ A.divisorDatum.pieces (σ y)) :
323	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
324	      (A.divisorDatum.sectionLocalEquations A.canonSection 𝒲 σ hσ
325	        (fun j y hy => A.germ_component_canonSection_mem_nonZeroDivisors j y hy))
326	      d := by
327	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ d.cover, fun x => inf_le_left, fun x => inf_le_right, fun x => ?_⟩
328	  -- the piece through `x` sits inside the adaptation piece of its lowered index
329	  have hpc : 𝒲.opens x ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) :=
330	    (hσ x).trans (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
331	  have hle : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x
332	      ≤ A.pieces (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) ⊓ d.cover.opens x :=
333	    inf_le_inf_right _ hpc
334	  refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hle (A.relUnit (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x), ?_⟩
335	  -- the defining equation of the comparison unit, restricted to the refinement
336	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom hle)
337	    (A.res_eqn_eq_relUnit_mul (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)) x)
338	  rw [map_mul] at key
339	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
340	  -- collapse the constructed datum's restricted equation onto the adaptation
341	  -- equation, term-mode (`rw` walks into the relCurve spelling seam — I-0237(a))
342	  have hlhs := (Scheme.resHom_resHom (hσ x)
343	      (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)
344	      (A.divisorDatum.component A.canonSection (σ x))).trans
345	    ((congrArg ((relCurve C R).resHom
346	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x)))
347	      (A.component_canonSection (σ x))).trans
348	      (Scheme.resHom_resHom (le_of_eq (A.thetaIdealDatum_pieces 0 (σ x)))
349	        ((inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x).trans (hσ x))
350	        (A.eqn (A.lowerIndex 0 (σ x)))))
351	  exact hlhs.trans key

58	/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/
59	private lemma val_unitsRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U)
60	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
61	    ((X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = X.resHom h (u : Γ(X, U)) :=

64	section AffineHom

66	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
67	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
68	variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
69	variable (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
70	variable (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
71	
72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
73	of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom

8	/-!
9	# Local equations for effective Cartier divisors and their Čech Picard class
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, an *effective Cartier divisor* is cut out, locally, by a single
12	regular equation. This file packages this data adapted to the pointed covers of the
13	Čech Picard group (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic`) and turns it into a Picard class.
14	
15	## Sign / normalization convention
16	
17	A local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective divisor `D` — one regular section `fᵢ`
18	on each member `𝒰 i` of a pointed cover, agreeing up to a unit on overlaps — is the
19	data of a trivialization of the invertible sheaf `𝒪(D)`: on `𝒰 i` the sheaf `𝒪(D)` is
20	trivialized by multiplication by `fᵢ`. The resulting transition units are
21	
22	`g i j = fᵢ / fⱼ ∈ Γ(X, 𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒰 j)ˣ`,
23	
24	i.e. the unique unit with `fᵢ|∩ = g i j · fⱼ|∩`. The class of the corresponding Čech
25	1-cocycle is `𝒪(D)`; this is `Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass`.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations`: local-equation data for an effective
30	  Cartier divisor adapted to a pointed cover — a regular section on each member, with
31	  the overlap ratios being units.
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: the
33	  section-level regularity consequence — every restriction of an equation to a sub-open
34	  is a nonzerodivisor.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.ratioUnit`, `ratioUnit_unique`,
36	  `ratioUnit_trans`: the transition units `g i j = fᵢ / fⱼ`, their uniqueness (from
37	  regularity), and the cocycle identity on triple overlaps.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.unitsCocycle`,
39	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass`: the Čech 1-cocycle `g i j` and its
40	  Picard class `𝒪(D)`.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.restrict` with `picClass_restrict`: refining
42	  the cover does not change the class.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.mul` with `picClass_mul`: the pointwise product
44	  of local equations realizes the product of Picard classes `𝒪(D) · 𝒪(D')`.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.rescale` with `picClass_rescale`: multiplying
46	  the equations by units does not change the class — `𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor.
47	-/

107	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor on `X`, adapted to a pointed cover:
108	a section `eqn x` on each member `cover.opens x`, whose germ at every point of that member
109	is a nonzerodivisor (`regular`) and whose overlap ratios `eqn x / eqn y` are units
110	(`ratio_isUnit`). The class of the associated Čech cocycle of transition units is the
111	divisor class `𝒪(D)`, see `LocalEquations.picClass`. -/
112	structure LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
113	  /-- The pointed cover on whose members the local equations live. -/
114	  cover : X.PointedCover
115	  /-- The local equation on the member `cover.opens x`. -/
116	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
117	  /-- Each local equation is regular: its germ at every point of its member is a
118	  nonzerodivisor in the stalk. This is the primitive form of regularity; it implies the
119	  regularity of every restriction (`eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). -/
120	  regular : ∀ (x y : X) (hy : y ∈ cover.opens x),
121	    (X.presheaf.germ (cover.opens x) y hy).hom (eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)
122	  /-- On the overlap `cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y` the two equations differ by a unit
123	  factor `eqn x = u · eqn y`, so that `𝒪(D)` is invertible. -/
124	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, ∃ u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y)ˣ,
125	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn x)
126	      = (u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y))
127	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (eqn y)

137	lemma eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors (x : X) {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ d.cover.opens x) :
138	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
139	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
140	  intro t ht

142	  intro y hy
143	  rw [map_zero]
144	  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t
145	      * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x)) = 0 := by
146	    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
147	  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at key
148	  exact (mul_left_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (d.regular x y (hW hy))).mp
149	    (by rw [mul_comm] at key; exact key)

154	`eqn x|∩ = g x y · eqn y|∩`. -/
155	noncomputable def ratioUnit (x y : X) : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ :=

159	`eqn x = g x y · eqn y`. -/
160	lemma eqn_restrict_eq (x y : X) :
161	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
162	      = (d.ratioUnit x y : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
163	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y) :=

167	overlap equals `g x y`. Regularity of `eqn y` (its restriction is a nonzerodivisor) makes

169	lemma ratioUnit_unique (x y : X) (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ)
170	    (hu : (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
171	      = (u : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
172	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)) :
173	    u = d.ratioUnit x y := by
174	  refine Units.ext ?_
175	  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
176	    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors y (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y
177	      ≤ d.cover.opens y))).mp ?_
178	  rw [← hu, d.eqn_restrict_eq x y]

181	`𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y ⊓ 𝒰z`: `g x y · g y z = g x z`. Proved by multiplying through by the regular
182	`eqn z` and cancelling. Mirrors `Scheme.unitsEvInf_trans`. -/
183	lemma ratioUnit_trans (x y z : X) :
184	    X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
185	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
186	            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)
187	        (d.ratioUnit x y)
188	      * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
189	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
190	            ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
191	          (d.ratioUnit y z)
192	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
193	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
194	            ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)
195	          (d.ratioUnit x z) := by
196	  refine Units.ext ?_

198	  rw [Units.val_mul, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict]
199	  -- cancel the regular restriction of `eqn z`
200	  refine (mul_cancel_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors
201	    (d.eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors z (inf_le_right :
202	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z ≤ d.cover.opens z))).mp ?_
203	  -- `g x z · eqn z = eqn x` on the triple overlap
204	  have hA := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
205	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
206	        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens z)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x z)

208	  -- `g y z · eqn z = eqn y` on the triple overlap
209	  have hB := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
210	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
211	        ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq y z)
212	  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at hB
213	  -- `g x y · eqn y = eqn x` on the triple overlap
214	  have hC := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
215	      d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d.cover.opens z
216	        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
217	  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at hC
218	  rw [mul_assoc, ← hB, ← hC]

221	/-! ## The cocycle and its Picard class -/
222	
223	/-- The Čech 1-cocycle of transition units `g x y = eqn x / eqn y` of a local-equation
224	system. -/
225	noncomputable def unitsCocycle : X.unitsCocycle d.cover :=
226	  OneCocycle.ofPairs (G := X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) (U := d.cover.opens)
227	    (fun x y ↦ d.ratioUnit x y) (fun x y z ↦ d.ratioUnit_trans x y z)
228	
229	@[simp]
230	lemma unitsCocycle_evInf (x y : X) :
231	    unitsEvInf d.unitsCocycle x y = d.ratioUnit x y :=
232	  OneCocycle.ofPairs_evInf (G := X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
233	    (U := d.cover.opens) (fun x y ↦ d.ratioUnit x y)
234	    (fun x y z ↦ d.ratioUnit_trans x y z) x y

236	/-- The Picard class `𝒪(D)` of a local-equation system for the effective divisor `D`:
237	the Čech class of the cocycle of transition units. -/
238	noncomputable def picClass : X.CechPic :=
239	  CechPic.mk d.cover d.unitsCocycle.class

241	/-! ## Refinement of the cover -/
242	
243	/-- The defining ratio equation of the restricted system, phrased on the underlying
244	restricted sections. -/
245	private lemma restrict_ratio_eq (𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (h : 𝒱 ≤ d.cover) (x y : X) :
246	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : 𝒱.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens y ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom
247	        ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h x)).op).hom (d.eqn x))
248	      = (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y)) (d.ratioUnit x y) : Γ(X, 𝒱.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens y))
249	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : 𝒱.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens y ≤ 𝒱.opens y)).op).hom
250	            ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h y)).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
251	  have E := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y))).op).hom
252	    (d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
253	  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at E
254	  rw [coe_unitsRestrict, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp]
255	  exact E

257	/-- Restriction of a local-equation system along a refinement `𝒱 ≤ d.cover`: restrict each
258	equation to the smaller member. Regularity restricts because germs factor through
259	restriction; the transition units restrict likewise. -/
260	def restrict (𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (h : 𝒱 ≤ d.cover) : X.LocalEquations where
261	  cover := 𝒱
262	  eqn x := (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h x)).op).hom (d.eqn x)
263	  regular x y hy := by
264	    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
265	    exact d.regular x y (h x hy)
266	  ratio_isUnit x y :=
267	    ⟨X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y)) (d.ratioUnit x y), d.restrict_ratio_eq 𝒱 h x y⟩
268	
269	/-- The transition units of the restricted system are the restrictions of the original
270	transition units. -/
271	lemma restrict_ratioUnit (𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (h : 𝒱 ≤ d.cover) (x y : X) :
272	    (d.restrict 𝒱 h).ratioUnit x y = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y)) (d.ratioUnit x y) :=
273	  ((d.restrict 𝒱 h).ratioUnit_unique x y _ (d.restrict_ratio_eq 𝒱 h x y)).symm
274	
275	/-- The refined local-equation system has the same Picard class: its cocycle is the
276	restriction of the original cocycle, and restriction stabilizes the Čech class. -/
277	@[simp]
278	lemma picClass_restrict (𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (h : 𝒱 ≤ d.cover) :
279	    (d.restrict 𝒱 h).picClass = d.picClass := by
280	  have hco : (d.restrict 𝒱 h).unitsCocycle
281	      = d.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)) := by
282	    refine unitsCocycle_ext fun x y ↦ ?_
283	    calc unitsEvInf (d.restrict 𝒱 h).unitsCocycle x y
284	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y)) (d.ratioUnit x y) :=
285	          ((d.restrict 𝒱 h).unitsCocycle_evInf x y).trans (d.restrict_ratioUnit 𝒱 h x y)
286	      _ = unitsEvInf (d.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x))) x y :=
287	          ((res_unitsEvInf h d.unitsCocycle x y).trans
288	            (congrArg (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (h x) (h y))) (d.unitsCocycle_evInf x y))).symm
289	  change CechPic.mk 𝒱 (d.restrict 𝒱 h).unitsCocycle.class = d.picClass
290	  rw [hco]
291	  exact CechPic.mk_unitsRes h d.unitsCocycle.class

293	/-! ## Product of local-equation systems (tensor product of divisor classes) -/
294	
295	/-- The defining ratio equation for the pointwise product of two local-equation systems,
296	on the common refinement `d.cover ⊓ d'.cover`. -/
297	private lemma mul_ratio_eq (d d' : X.LocalEquations) (x y : X) :
298	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
299	        (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)
300	          ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x)).op).hom
301	        ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
302	              d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x ≤ d.cover.opens x)).op).hom (d.eqn x)
303	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
304	              d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x ≤ d'.cover.opens x)).op).hom (d'.eqn x))
305	      = ((X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left) (d.ratioUnit x y)
306	            * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right) (d'.ratioUnit x y)
307	          : Γ(X, (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y))ˣ)
308	          : Γ(X, (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)))
309	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
310	            (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)
311	              ≤ d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)).op).hom
312	            ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
313	                  d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y)
314	              * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
315	                  d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y ≤ d'.cover.opens y)).op).hom
316	                  (d'.eqn y)) := by
317	  have Ed := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left :
318	      (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)
319	        ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
320	  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at Ed
321	  have Ed' := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right :
322	      (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x) ⊓ (d.cover.opens y ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)
323	        ≤ d'.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d'.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
324	  rw [map_mul, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp] at Ed'
325	  rw [Units.val_mul, coe_unitsRestrict, coe_unitsRestrict, map_mul, map_mul,
326	    sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp, sectionRestrict_comp,
327	    Ed, Ed']
328	  exact mul_mul_mul_comm _ _ _ _

330	/-- The pointwise product of two local-equation systems, on the common refinement
331	`d.cover ⊓ d'.cover`: multiply the equations. It cuts out the sum of the two divisors, and
332	its Picard class is the product `𝒪(D) · 𝒪(D')`. -/
333	def mul (d d' : X.LocalEquations) : X.LocalEquations where
334	  cover := d.cover ⊓ d'.cover
335	  eqn x := (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
336	        d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x ≤ d.cover.opens x)).op).hom (d.eqn x)
337	      * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
338	          d.cover.opens x ⊓ d'.cover.opens x ≤ d'.cover.opens x)).op).hom (d'.eqn x)
339	  regular x y hy := by
340	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
341	    exact mul_mem (d.regular x y hy.1) (d'.regular x y hy.2)
342	  ratio_isUnit x y :=
343	    ⟨X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left) (d.ratioUnit x y)
344	        * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right) (d'.ratioUnit x y),
345	      mul_ratio_eq d d' x y⟩
346	
347	/-- The transition units of a product system are the products of the (restricted)
348	transition units. -/
349	lemma mul_ratioUnit (d d' : X.LocalEquations) (x y : X) :
350	    (d.mul d').ratioUnit x y
351	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left) (d.ratioUnit x y)
352	        * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right) (d'.ratioUnit x y) :=
353	  ((d.mul d').ratioUnit_unique x y _ (mul_ratio_eq d d' x y)).symm
354	
355	/-- The Picard class of a product of local-equation systems is the product of the Picard
356	classes: `𝒪(D + D') = 𝒪(D) · 𝒪(D')`. -/
357	@[simp]
358	lemma picClass_mul (d d' : X.LocalEquations) :
359	    (d.mul d').picClass = d.picClass * d'.picClass := by
360	  have hco : (d.mul d').unitsCocycle
361	      = d.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_left)
362	        * d'.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_right) := by
363	    refine unitsCocycle_ext fun x y ↦ ?_
364	    calc unitsEvInf (d.mul d').unitsCocycle x y
365	        = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left) (d.ratioUnit x y)
366	            * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right) (d'.ratioUnit x y) :=
367	          ((d.mul d').unitsCocycle_evInf x y).trans (mul_ratioUnit d d' x y)
368	      _ = unitsEvInf (d.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_left)
369	            * d'.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_right)) x y :=
370	          (congr_arg₂ (· * ·)
371	            ((res_unitsEvInf inf_le_left d.unitsCocycle x y).trans
372	              (congrArg (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_left inf_le_left))
373	                (d.unitsCocycle_evInf x y))).symm
374	            ((res_unitsEvInf inf_le_right d'.unitsCocycle x y).trans
375	              (congrArg (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_right))
376	                (d'.unitsCocycle_evInf x y))).symm).trans
377	            (mul_unitsEvInf (d.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_left))
378	              (d'.unitsCocycle.res (fun x ↦ homOfLE inf_le_right)) x y).symm
379	  have hclass : (d.mul d').unitsCocycle.class
380	      = unitsRes (inf_le_left : d.cover ⊓ d'.cover ≤ d.cover) d.unitsCocycle.class
381	        * unitsRes (inf_le_right : d.cover ⊓ d'.cover ≤ d'.cover) d'.unitsCocycle.class :=
382	    (congrArg OneCocycle.class hco).trans rfl
383	  change CechPic.mk (d.cover ⊓ d'.cover) (d.mul d').unitsCocycle.class
384	    = d.picClass * d'.picClass
385	  rw [hclass]
386	  change _ = CechPic.mk d.cover d.unitsCocycle.class * CechPic.mk d'.cover d'.unitsCocycle.class
387	  rw [CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf]

389	/-! ## Independence under unit rescaling -/
390	
391	/-- The defining ratio equation for a unitwise rescaling of a local-equation system. -/
392	private lemma rescale_ratio_eq (d : X.LocalEquations) (v : ∀ x, Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)ˣ)
393	    (x y : X) :
394	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
395	        d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens x)).op).hom
396	        ((v x : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)) * d.eqn x)
397	      = ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x) * d.ratioUnit x y
398	            * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y))⁻¹
399	          : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ)
400	          : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
401	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
402	            d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom
403	            ((v y : Γ(X, d.cover.opens y)) * d.eqn y) := by
404	  have key : (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x) * d.ratioUnit x y
405	        * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y))⁻¹) * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y)
406	      = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x) * d.ratioUnit x y := inv_mul_cancel_right _ _
407	  rw [map_mul, map_mul,
408	    ← coe_unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x), ← coe_unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y),
409	    d.eqn_restrict_eq x y, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, ← Units.val_mul, key]
410	
411	/-- A unitwise rescaling of a local-equation system: multiply each equation by a unit on
412	its member. It cuts out the same divisor. -/
413	def rescale (d : X.LocalEquations) (v : ∀ x, Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)ˣ) : X.LocalEquations where
414	  cover := d.cover
415	  eqn x := (v x : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)) * d.eqn x
416	  regular x y hy := by
417	    rw [map_mul]
418	    exact mul_mem
419	      (((v x).isUnit.map (X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
420	      (d.regular x y hy)
421	  ratio_isUnit x y :=
422	    ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x) * d.ratioUnit x y * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y))⁻¹,
423	      rescale_ratio_eq d v x y⟩
424	
425	/-- The transition units of a rescaled system, conjugated by the rescaling units. -/
426	lemma rescale_ratioUnit (d : X.LocalEquations) (v : ∀ x, Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)ˣ) (x y : X) :
427	    (d.rescale v).ratioUnit x y
428	      = X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x) * d.ratioUnit x y
429	        * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y))⁻¹ :=
430	  ((d.rescale v).ratioUnit_unique x y _ (rescale_ratio_eq d v x y)).symm
431	
432	/-- A commutative-group cancellation used for the rescaling coboundary. -/
433	private lemma inv_mul_mul_inv_cancel {G : Type u} [CommGroup G] (a r b : G) :
434	    a⁻¹ * (a * r * b⁻¹) = r * b⁻¹ := by
435	  rw [mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel_left]
436	
437	/-- The coboundary identity witnessing that rescaling does not change the Picard class:
438	the `0`-cochain `v⁻¹` conjugates the rescaled cocycle into the original. -/
439	private lemma rescale_coboundary (d : X.LocalEquations) (v : ∀ x, Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)ˣ)
440	    (x y : X) :
441	    X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x)⁻¹ * (d.rescale v).ratioUnit x y
442	      = d.ratioUnit x y * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y)⁻¹ :=
443	  (congrArg (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x)⁻¹ * ·) (rescale_ratioUnit d v x y)).trans
444	    (inv_mul_mul_inv_cancel (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x)) (d.ratioUnit x y)
445	      (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y)))
446	
447	/-- Unitwise rescaling does not change the Picard class: `𝒪(D)` depends only on the
448	divisor, not on the chosen local equations. -/
449	@[simp]
450	lemma picClass_rescale (d : X.LocalEquations) (v : ∀ x, Γ(X, d.cover.opens x)ˣ) :
451	    (d.rescale v).picClass = d.picClass := by
452	  have hcoh : (d.rescale v).unitsCocycle.IsCohomologous d.unitsCocycle :=
453	    unitsCocycle_isCohomologous (fun x ↦ (v x)⁻¹) fun x y ↦
454	      ((congrArg (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (v x)⁻¹ * ·)
455	          ((d.rescale v).unitsCocycle_evInf x y)).trans
456	        (rescale_coboundary d v x y)).trans
457	          (congrArg (· * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (v y)⁻¹) (d.unitsCocycle_evInf x y).symm)
458	  change CechPic.mk d.cover (d.rescale v).unitsCocycle.class
459	    = CechPic.mk d.cover d.unitsCocycle.class
460	  exact congrArg (CechPic.mk d.cover) hcoh.class_eq
